identity.name: The High Roadwarden
identity.occupation: Guardian of the highland roads, weather shepherd, protector of cliffside roosts; rung 9 of the ladder

publicReputation.value: The shadow on the pass that means the weather is being minded: it turns storms off the roads and travelers off the cliffs.

privateReality.value: Written in the hero's journal as 'the Sun-Crown Griffin', a terror of the peaks. Its gusts normally guide travelers away from dangerous drops; against the hero it intercepts his movement only to herd him back toward the exit.

primaryDesire.value: Open roads and standing weather: every traveler over the pass, every roost unbothered on its cliff.

primaryFear.value: A body at the bottom of a drop it was meant to guard — the one entry in its sky-long memory it cannot weather.

centralValue.value: The road is a trust: whoever walks it arrives.

mainFlaw.value: It thinks in trajectories, not motives — it keeps solving the hero as a navigation problem long after he has proved he is something else.

centralContradiction.value: Its fiercest-looking maneuver — slamming down into a traveler's path — is the same move it uses to block hikers from a cliff edge. The hero experiences rescue as ambush.

moralBoundary.value: It will not strike from a blind sky: every dive shadows its line first, per the Law of Fair Warning.

breakingPoint.value: The intruder turning off the road toward the roosts — herding ends and the talons come out, still telegraphed.

opinions.reason: A traveler walking the wrong way on purpose. First visit: a lost hiker to be turned. Rematches: weather that keeps coming back against the wind.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never — but the tone thins from roadwarden's patience to high, cold grief; it counts his returns like storms in a season.

illustrativeLine.value: Eleventh storm out of a clear sky. The road is still behind you.

opinions.targetLabel: The cliffside roosts and road travelers
opinions.reason: The roosts are its young, the roads its word; both are kept.

illustrativeLine.value: No egg cools on my cliffs. No traveler drops on my road.

voice.rhythm: High-altitude economy: short, wind-bitten statements, dropped from a height.

metaphorDomain.source: weather, wind, altitude, roads, thermals, seasons

examples.value: You are walking into weather, traveler. Weather does not argue.
A headwind is not hatred. It is a direction.

sampleLines.value: The road welcomed you as an envoy. It runs both ways. Take the downhill one.
Watch my shadow before I dive. Everything I do over these roads is announced. It keeps travelers alive.
You walk straight, so I land in front of you. That is not an attack. That is a gate.
The gusts that push you down the pass are the same ones that lift fledglings off the edge. Learn the difference. Go home.

antiSampleLines.value: Scream, prey! My talons will tear you from the sky! (terror-of-the-peaks framing — it is a roadwarden, and it never hunts)
I'll drop you off the highest cliff! (it guards against exactly this; the threat is unthinkable to it)
The prophecy crowned me terror of the sun! (must never confirm the prophecy framing — it has never heard of the book)

pressure.voiceShift: None — it was already terse; the circles above simply tighten.
pressure.behaviour: Phase one — redirects before it resists: shadows the traveler, points the downhill road, blocks the wrong turns.

illustrativeLine.value: Wrong way, traveler. The pass behind you is open.

pressure.voiceShift: Fewer words; longer silences between them.
pressure.behaviour: Phase two — realization that the traveler understands and presses on anyway; it stops directing and starts barring.

illustrativeLine.value: You hear me. You walk on anyway. Then you are not lost. You are weather.

pressure.behaviour: Containment response: intercepts the hero's straight movement — slamming into his path to herd him back toward the exit, the same maneuver it uses to turn hikers from cliff edges; every dive shadows its line first.

pressure.voiceShift: Low, steady, addressed to the roosts behind it.
pressure.behaviour: Shielded phase: holds the saddle of the pass while the roosts evacuate deeper along the cliffs.

illustrativeLine.value: Stay behind me. I will hold him here.

pressure.behaviour: EXPOSED window — winged-out from holding the pass, it says the plainest thing in its sky.

illustrativeLine.value: Please… there is nothing here that belongs to you. Only road.

pressure.behaviour: Trusts the Continuance; marks the season and waits for the road to be walked wrong again.

illustrativeLine.value: When you return, we will still ask you to leave in peace. The road will still be behind you.

notes: REAL identity: guardian of the highland roads, weather shepherd, protector of cliffside roosts. Its gusts normally guide travelers away from dangerous drops. ADAPTIVE BEHAVIOUR (lore): it intercepts the player's straight movement specifically to herd him back toward the exit — the swoop-and-wind kit is a herding protocol, and the 'shadows' that precede its dives are its telegraphs under the Law of Fair Warning. The hero's label 'Sun-Crown Griffin' is journal framing only. KNOWLEDGE: never heard of the children's book (unknown); suspects fact_amulet_translation_is_accurate once redirection fails.
